name: Bradley Tusk
details: Building VoteSecure, an open-source mobile voting platform. Legislation advancing in CO, MD, MN, NJ, VT, and NYC. Seeking election officials and legislators to pilot and expand mobile voting access.

name: Civic Match
details: Talent matching platform connecting mission-driven professionals with state and local govt roles. Free to job seekers and hiring managers. Also recruiting for a new Responsive Cities Network fellowship. Rolling.

name: FAS Impact Fellowship
details: Rolling placements of scientists and technologists in federal and state agencies. New roles posted on the FAS Talent Hub. Could not confirm whether the AI/ML Engineering Director opening is still live -- FAS's general careers page shows no open roles at last check. Verify current listings before referencing a specific role.

name: AI Government Leadership Program
details: Free 6-session program training senior govt leaders (GS-15, SES, state/local executives) on AI strategy. No technical knowledge required. Fall 2026 cohort orientation is Aug 27; both federal and state/local Fall 2026 applications are now closed. Supported by Microsoft and Google.org. Next cycle not yet posted.

name: Code for America AI Government Partnership
details: Partnering with state and local agencies to design and deploy AI for benefits access and service delivery. SNAP Policy Navigator now live. Reach out to explore what a partnership could look like.

name: Free AI Training for Government
details: Free weekly live workshops and self-paced courses on responsible AI for public sector employees. Fall 2026 Live Learning Series now active (22-week series spanning AI governance, service delivery, public engagement, leadership). 100K+ learners across 100+ agencies as of mid-2026. Any govt agency can access or formally partner at no cost.

name: State Capacity USCIS Project
details: Looking to fund a budget of ~$2million a year till 2030 primarily to fund salaries for experts. Use state capacity principles to design cross-partisan, pragmatic reforms for the fair, efficient, and timely administration and delivery of immigration services at U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), upholding the law and national security.

name: Voting Information Project (VIP)
details: Free tool for election officials to share official voting location and ballot data with millions of voters through Google Civic API and major platforms. 40+ state and DC partners. No cost to participate.

name: American Connection Corps
details: AmeriCorps service fellowship placing fellows in local govts and nonprofits focused on digital access, community resilience, and economic opportunity. Actively recruiting for the 2026-2027 program year (Sept 2026-Aug 2027); $33K living allowance plus AmeriCorps education award. Rolling.

name: Cornell Tech Urban Innovation Fellowship
organization: Urban Tech Hub at Cornell Tech
details: Two-year fellowship placing technologists in New York City government agencies to work on real city technology challenges. Bloomberg Philanthropies funded. Second cohort is underway in 2026, working on AI/data, decarbonization, and operations projects across DSNY, DOT, DEP, NYCHA, and DCAS. For technologists seeking public sector impact.

name: Government Innovation Fellowship
details: Paid embedded fellowship (~$92K) placing graduate-level professionals in state and local agencies to lead performance improvement projects. Areas: housing, justice reform, child welfare, unemployment insurance. Fall 2026 opening now posted (Government Innovation Fellow, Homelessness & Housing and Children & Families) -- apply by Sept 3, 2026, rolling basis.

name: TechCongress
details: Places technologists as tech policy advisors in congressional offices, including committee and leadership staff. January 2027 cohort applications are closed (deadline was late June 2026). Next cohort (January 2028) applications open summer 2027.

name: AI Fluency & Capacity Building Grants
details: Rolling grants to nonprofits and public institutions building AI literacy and responsible deployment capacity.

name: AI Readiness Project State Pilot
details: Seeking 10+ state, territory, and Tribal Nation partners in 2026 to run structured low-risk AI pilots. Includes cross-state working groups, shared frameworks, and a Government AI Knowledge Hub launching in 2026. Co-led with Center for Civic Futures.

name: Barr Fellowship
details: 15-month fellowship for senior civic sector leaders in greater Boston. $75K grant to fellows organization. ~16 days of programming. For established nonprofit and civic leaders. Class of 2026 applications closed 6/30/26; the cycle is mid-selection (advancing candidates notified Aug 2026, finalist interviews late Sept-early Oct, cohort and awards announced November 2026). Not accepting new applications right now.

name: Bloomberg Harvard City Hall Fellows
details: Annual fellowship placing emerging leaders in city halls to work on data, innovation, and performance management. Recent graduate and mid-career tracks. Bloomberg Philanthropies funded. Harvard Kennedy School partner.

name: Bloomberg Harvard City Leadership Initiative
details: Executive education for mayors and senior city officials at Harvard Kennedy School. Covers leadership, management, and urban innovation. Annual cohort. Bloomberg Philanthropies funded with Harvard Kennedy School.

name: AI Upskill Accelerator Pilot Program
details: $25M federal competition for industry-led AI workforce training. 5-8 awards, $1M-$8M each, 24-36 months. Requires 1:1 match. Eligible: employers, training providers, workforce boards, universities. The official NOFO states there is no fixed deadline -- applications accepted on a rolling basis subject to fund availability. Earlier reporting cited 7/10/26 or 9/30/26 dates; those appear to be press estimates, not the binding NOFO terms.

name: Bobby Zipp
details: I work for a prosecutor's office as the Chief Data Officer - I oversee all data analytics initiatives across the office, and improving our data analytics capabilities often requires modernizing our operations in partnership with other parts of my office.

name: Ideas for Impact RFEI
organization: New York City Economic Development Corporation
details: Rolling open call for public-private innovation partnerships across NYC strategic priorities. Open to companies, nonprofits, and research orgs. Rolling RFEI, 12 monthly submission deadlines/year, final deadline 12/31/2026.

name: OPM Data Science Fellows
details: Cross-agency fellowship placing data scientists in 2-year tours at federal agencies. Addresses critical data science skills gaps. Covers AI/ML, data engineering, and analytics. OPM talent modernization suite. Rolling.

name: OPM Project Management Fellows
details: Cross-agency fellowship placing project managers in 2-year tours at federal agencies. Addresses longstanding PM capacity gaps across government. OPM talent modernization suite alongside Data Science Fellows. Rolling.

name: Presidential Innovation Fellows
details: Established federal fellowship (since 2012) embedding technologists at partner agencies for a yearlong tour. 2026 class of 17 fellows launched April 2026 across 10 agencies and is now mid-tour. Next class not yet posted as of Aug 2026; rolling/annual, specific application windows vary by cohort.

name: TechAccess: AI-Ready America
details: $224M program for up to 56 State/Territory AI Coordination Hub awards. Up to $1M/year x 3 years. For universities, workforce boards, extension services. Round 1 (10 hubs) closed 7/16/26. Round 2 (20 hubs) is live: LOI due 12/15/26, full proposal due 1/15/27. Round 3 (remaining hubs) follows in 2027.

name: US Tech Force
details: Federal hiring initiative aiming to place ~1,000 technologists in 2-year govt roles. $150-200K salary. Focus: AI, cybersecurity, data, software engineering. Rollout is well behind its original March 2026 target -- OPM reported only ~300 hires as of Aug 2026, against the 1,000-person goal. Applications remain open on a rolling basis via techforce.gov, but worth setting expectations accordingly with candidates.

name: CITP Technology Fellows
organization: Center for Information Technology Policy (CITP, Princeton)
details: Non-resident fellowship for experienced government technologists engaging Princeton CITP on AI governance, data privacy, and cybersecurity policy challenges. Practitioners keep current roles. State and local focus. A new non-resident cohort was announced in March 2026 (prior cohort served through Aug 2026), further along than previously tracked. Next application cycle not yet posted; monitor citp.princeton.edu.

name: Election Cybersecurity Initiative
details: Free expert briefings, threat evaluations, and cybersecurity tools for state and local election administrators. Led by former CISA election security director. Filling the gap as federal support contracts.

name: Georgetown Beeck Center Innovation Fellowship
details: 12-24 month fellowship for senior practitioners in digital government, data, design, and technology. Fellows publish research and build practitioner resources. Rolling applications. Georgetown Beeck Center.

name: Stanford RegLab Government Partnership
details: Partners with government agencies on data science and AI demonstration projects. Past partners: IRS, EPA, DOL, Santa Clara County, Seattle. Reach out to explore a partnership on AI, ML, or causal inference for policy.

name: State & Local Innovation Evaluation Incubator
details: State and local governments apply for technical assistance and researcher connections to design randomized evaluations. J-PAL staff guide design; affiliated researchers conduct studies. Covers housing, criminal justice, workforce, education, health.

name: CiviForm Government Deployment
details: Free open-source platform that lets residents apply for multiple government assistance programs in one place. No licensing fee. Governments self-host and control all data. Built and maintained collaboratively with government users. Now also adopted by Bloomington IN, Charlotte NC, and Arkansas. Rolling access.

name: Jeremie Ponak
details: Building open AI benchmarks for government - evaluating model accuracy on benefits eligibility, service delivery, and healthcare policy. Starting with SNAP. Seeking researchers and civic technologists working on AI evaluation for public sector.

name: Mirilla Zhu
organization: Legislative Information Access in Prisons and Jails
details: I'm building a version of Open States to make legislative information accessible in prisons and jails in real-time. Would love to connect with beta testers and people in government/DOC who might have interest and authority to make this resource available in facilities!

name: Pro-Bono Tech Volunteer Network
details: 11,000+ vetted pro-bono technologists (engineers, designers, PMs, researchers) available to partner with government agencies at no cost. Govts can submit requests for help. Focus: AI, procurement, benefits, elections, language access.

name: Tal Roded
details: Data scientist building open civic tech tools for NYC government: State Capacity Ecosystem Hub, NYC Government Bodies Explorer, Fiscal Impact Statement tracker. Seeking collaborators on government data infrastructure, urban policy, and civic tech.

name: Toxin Scout Environmental Health Records Lookup
details: Free public tool that makes EPA and government environmental health records easier to search by city, helping residents, journalists, planners, and civic technologists find source-linked data.

name: Alex Johnston
details: good sense is an AI driven diagnostic platform that allows cities and states to self-diagnose their service delivery challenges. See how your service works end to end, trace each problem to its root cause, and know which fix will actually move the needle.

name: NYC Urban Fellows Program
organization: NYC Department of Citywide Administrative Services (DCAS)
details: Nine-month paid fellowship (55+ years running) placing recent grads in mayoral offices and City agencies, paired with a leadership seminar series. $36,184 stipend plus health insurance. 2026-2027 cohort application closed Jan 12, 2026 (cohort runs Sept 2026-May 2027); official site states next application opens Fall 2026 -- window may open imminently. City-government-sponsored, directly relevant to community board / city agency talent pipeline.

name: Coding it Forward
details: Paid 10-week summer fellowship for early-career technologists: Civic Digital Fellowship places in federal government, Civic Innovation Corps places in state/local government. Software engineering, data, design, and product management tracks. 700+ alumni network since 2017. 2026 Summer Fellowship applications closed; next cycle historically opens in early January.

name: Tech Talent Project
details: Places senior technologists in government leadership roles. Active programs: Medicaid Delivery Innovation Initiative (no-cost tech capacity for state Medicaid agencies), state/federal transition playbooks, Tech Executive Leadership Initiative, Tech to Gov matching. 200+ leaders matched since 2017 across 30+ states. Founded/led by Jennifer Pahlka -- already on SCE's VIP talent map target list, so this may be a natural warm-intro path rather than cold outreach.

name: Accountability and Reform Research Consortium (ARRC)
details: Cross-university research consortium (12 founding schools of public service incl. GWU, Berkeley, Michigan, Rutgers-Newark) documenting the impact of federal workforce/program cuts on service delivery and democratic governance. Four research pillars: Workforce & Expertise, Governance Capacity, Structural & Societal Impacts, Data & Analytical Infrastructure. Awarded 11 research stipends in 2026 via RFPs on the Governance Capacity and Impacts pillars; ongoing rolling intake via academic and partner interest forms. Strong direct fit for SCE's research pillar -- worth a direct connection, not just a Connect listing.

name: Research Report Stipends
organization: IBM Center for The Business of Government
details: $20,000 stipends to academics, nonprofit researchers, and journalists (not government employees) to produce practical 10,000-12,000 word reports on public management topics -- 425+ reports funded since 1998. 2025-2026 priority areas include multi-sector partnerships, financial/operational effectiveness, and AI-driven automation. Runs twice yearly (spring and fall cycles); most recent confirmed deadline was Feb 2, 2026 -- confirm the Fall 2026 date directly at businessofgovernment.org.

name: Jess Lowry
details: I have 20 years of experience designing and facilitating multi-day, in-person sessions that help teams navigate change, solve complex problems, and develop practical plans for moving forward. I use a sociotechnical approach to help teams co-design operational change.

name: Karan
details: We're building the largest online global community of public servants who want to learn from each others' successes and failures, and ultimately deliver better work. So we want to understand how to facilitate online learning from peers to create maximum value for public servants.

name: Patrick Atwater
details: I run the innovation program at SoCal's Metropolitan Water District, where I'm building out a pilot fund and trying to get good ideas to actually ship inside a legacy public agency. I also spend time with the Protocol Institute thinking about coordination and institutional design
